prs.title: fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash

merge_commit_fingerprint.message:
fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash (#2767)

* fix(capture): end special-scheme URL authorities at a backslash

The native mitmproxy adapter removed transport userinfo with
`^(...//)[^/?#]*@`, so the authority ran to the last "@" before "/", "?"
or "#". For `https://example.test\part@tail` it treated
`example.test\part` as userinfo, reported `https://tail` as the
Location, and withdrew the original bytes as a transport credential.
WHATWG URL parsing, used by the shared TypeScript owner
(recordedTransportUrl.ts) and by HAR captures, ends a special-scheme or
scheme-relative authority at a backslash, so that "@" is ordinary path
text.

Locate the authority with the same boundary rule before removing
userinfo. Bytes are handled as Latin-1 text so unrelated bytes stay
identical. Userinfo before the backslash is still removed and redacted.
Add source unit tests for the adapter projection to test:python.

Fixes #2671

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): skip special-scheme leading slashes before userinfo

Ending the authority at a backslash exposed a credential: for
`https://\user:pass@host/path`, WHATWG parsing skips every leading "/"
or "\" after a special scheme (and in scheme-relative references), so
`user:pass` is userinfo, but the new boundary stopped at the first
backslash and found no "@". The same applied to `https:\\user:pass@host`
and `https:user:pass@host`.

Start the authority after that whole slash run for non-file special
schemes and scheme-relative references. File URLs keep their "//"
boundary because they carry no userinfo. Load the adapter in tests with
fresh mitmproxy stand-ins scoped to its import instead of leaving them
in sys.modules.

* fix(capture): keep URLs that WHATWG rejects instead of redacting userinfo

File URLs cannot carry userinfo (an "@" in a file host fails the parse),
and a special authority whose host or port WHATWG rejects fails the whole
URL. Neither has credentials, so the bridge now keeps their source text
and byte sidecar. Checked against Node's URL over 30,000 spellings: no
under-redaction, over-redaction 20,540 -> 5,865 (remaining: empty
userinfo, IPv4 range, IDNA, non-special and baseless references).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): strip trailing URL whitespace and validate IP hosts and ports

The previous host check counted trailing C0 controls and spaces, which
WHATWG strips, so `https://user:pw@host ` kept its password. Trailing
C0/space is now removed from the parse view (raw offsets are unchanged).

Special hosts now also follow the WHATWG IPv4 parser (ends-in-a-number,
hex/octal parts, range) and IPv6 literal syntax (zone IDs rejected), and
ports are bounded lexically before int(), which raised ValueError past
4300 digits on Python 3.11+ and failed the whole capture.

Node URL differential over 126,000 spellings: under-redaction 8,084 -> 0,
ValueError 2,550 -> 0; remaining special-scheme over-redaction is IDNA
and the pinned empty-userinfo case. Cost: +0.6 us per URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(capture): redact userinfo before hosts that need Unicode mapping

A non-ASCII special host may map under UTS #46 to an accepted host
(fullwidth digits, ideographic full stops, ignored code points), so
treat it as accepted instead of running the ASCII IPv4 check on it.

fix(uninstall): remove the REA-owned ZCode fallback registration (#2783)

* fix(uninstall): remove the REA-owned ZCode fallback registration

ZCode loads the user-scope `~/.agents/mcp.json` `mcpServers` fallback
whenever its native `mcp.servers` table is empty. Uninstall removed REA
only from the native table, so a REA-owned fallback entry became eligible
to load again once the last native server was gone, while uninstall
reported ZCode as removed and complete.

configuration in the uninstall host. It goes through the same
ownership check, `.rea.backup`, readback and restore path as every other
client configuration, so other fallback servers and settings, and a
foreign `rea` entry, are preserved. Its result merges into the ZCode item.

prs.title: fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections

merge_commit_fingerprint.message:
fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections (#2705)

* fix(electron): reject non-executable paths and contain launch rejections

An executable_path that runs but never prints the inspector line made
Playwright's electron.launch() leave three waits unawaited. They rejected
unhandled and Node ended the CLI or the MCP server (#2269).

Check the resolved executable_path is a regular file, and on non-Windows
hosts that it passes X_OK, before any launch. Wrap only the launch call
in a scoped unhandledRejection listener that absorbs rejections whose
stack is in playwright-core/lib and re-throws anything else.

Tested on Linux with Node 22.23.1, 24.18.0 and 26.11.1.

Refs #2269

🤖 Generated with Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5, verified by Opus 5.5) 🦊

* fix(electron): absorb only this launch's orphaned rejections

The listener around the launch dropped every rejection with a
playwright-core stack, so an unrelated Playwright failure during the
launch window would vanish. Hold those rejections instead. When the
launch settles, drop only the ones whose message is part of the launch's
own error (the orphans of a failed launch). Raise every other one again
through the unhandledRejection path, so the process still fails. A launch
that succeeds raises all of them. Rejections without a Playwright stack
still fail at once.

One setImmediate turn before the decision lets rejections queued by the
settling tick arrive first. It is a single turn, not a timer. A shared
set of absorbed errors stops overlapping launches from raising each
other's orphans. The listener is removed on every path.

Add child-process tests that drive the built provider through its launch
seam, since Vitest's worker has its own unhandledRejection listener.

fix(artifacts): preserve Mach-O load-command string identity (#2110)

* fix(artifacts): preserve Mach-O load-command string identity

* fix(process): report no remaining time after a provider deadline fires

Node timers can fire while performance.now() is still a fraction of a
millisecond short of the monotonic deadline. ProviderStartupDeadline then
reported interruption "timeout" and an aborted signal while remainingMs()
returned ceil(0.x) = 1, so polling loops guarded by remainingMs() > 0
(Hopper and Ghidra startup) could run past an elapsed deadline, and the
real-timer test "aborts a bounded wait when its real monotonic deadline
expires" failed intermittently in CI (expected 1 to be 0).

Once the deadline's own timer has classified a timeout, report zero
remaining time. A deterministic regression test fires the timer with the
monotonic clock 0.4 ms short of the deadline.

* fix(process): report no remaining time after a provider deadline fires

Node timers can fire while performance.now() is still a fraction of a
millisecond short of the monotonic deadline. ProviderStartupDeadline then
reported interruption "timeout" and an aborted signal while remainingMs()
returned ceil(0.x) = 1, so polling loops guarded by remainingMs() > 0
(Hopper and Ghidra startup) could run past an elapsed deadline, and the
real-timer test "aborts a bounded wait when its real monotonic deadline
expires" failed intermittently in CI (expected 1 to be 0).

Once the deadline's own timer has classified a timeout, report zero
remaining time. A deterministic regression test fires the timer with the
monotonic clock 0.4 ms short of the deadline.

merge_commit_fingerprint.message:
fix: preserve loading and cancellation state when restarting completion requests (#21228)

## Background

Restarting useCompletion immediately after stop() allowed the
replacement stream to continue while loading became false and subsequent
stop() calls could no longer cancel it.

## Root Cause

callCompletionApi unconditionally cleared shared loading, error,
completion, and abort-controller state when an older request settled.
Deterministic overlapping-request tests confirmed that aborted,
successful, and failed requests could overwrite state owned by a newer
request.

## Summary

Added request-ownership checks to callCompletionApi and updated React,
Vue, Svelte, and Angular completion integrations to retain the active
controller until its owning request settles. React now stores the
controller in a ref for synchronous cancellation.

## Testing

Added core regression coverage for text and data protocols across abort,
success, and error outcomes, plus a React hook test for stopping and
immediately restarting a request.

## End-to-end Validation

- `replay_original_reproduction`: the immutable reproduction completed
successfully across all protocols and outcomes; status was
`no-longer-reproduces`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21224

Closes #21226

prs.title: fix: TUI Backspace submits partial Unicode graphemes

merge_commit_fingerprint.message:
fix: TUI Backspace submits partial Unicode graphemes (#21229)

## Background

Backspace in published @ai-sdk/tui prompts could submit corrupted or
partial Unicode graphemes, including unpaired emoji surrogates and
incomplete combining or joined sequences.

## Root Cause

The Backspace handler used slice(0, -1), which removes one UTF-16 code
unit rather than one displayed grapheme. The reproduction confirmed
partial submissions for emoji, combining characters, and joined emoji
through both DEL and BS encodings.

## Summary

Changed prompt deletion to remove the final Intl.Segmenter grapheme
cluster, enabled the required Intl TypeScript library, removed
reproduction-only artifacts, and added a patch changeset.

## Testing

Added prompt submission regressions covering DEL and BS emoji deletion,
combining-character sequences, and joined emoji sequences.

## End-to-end Validation

- `pnpm -C examples/ai-functions exec tsx
src/reproduction/issue-21225-tui-backspace-grapheme.ts` via immutable
replay exited successfully and reported that the issue was not present.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21225

Closes #21227
